cer07.title: Re-decided obligations

cer07.metaRead: Read only for you. Operations officers resolve each one.
cer07.sortNote: Overdue first, then by due time.
cer07.endNote: Every follow-up is on this page.
cer07.endFiltered: Every follow-up that matches is on this page.

cer08.metaOpen: Due {due}. RightOne applies it when it is due unless you resolve it first.

cer08.help.END_AT_EFFECTIVE_DATE: The rule preselects End at the effective date because a condition of the amendment is not met.
cer08.help.NO_CHANGE_NEEDED: The rule preselects No change needed because the new decision keeps the same scope and dates.
cer08.help.REPLACE: The rule preselects Replace because the holder changes.
cer08.oAmendHelp: The record takes a period of {obd}, in force from the moment it is recorded.
cer08.oReplaceHelp: A new record for the new holder. This record’s period ends on {d}.
cer08.oEndHelp: This record’s period ends on {d}. A period under the new decision follows only once its conditions hold.
cer08.oNoneHelp: A period naming the new decision, with the same scope and dates.
cer08.reasonHelp: Kept with the follow-up. At most 2,000 characters.
cer08.wrong: With this outcome the record does not match the decision in force. Keep the outcome the rule preselected.

cer10.title: Status record signing keys
cer10.meta: Each printout is signed with the key in use when it is printed. A key is due to retire twelve months after it starts signing. The security administrator retires it by hand. As of {ts}.

cer10.sortNote: The key that signs now first, then by start time, latest first.
cer10.regDesc: The key service must already hold the key. RightOne signs a test payload with the handle and checks it with the public key before listing the key.
cer10.fKidHelp: Not used by any key so far.
cer10.fHandleHelp: The key service’s handle for the key.
cer10.fJwkHelp: A JSON Web Key on the P-256 curve.
cer10.fFromHelp: A future time, in Vietnam time.
cer10.kidExists: A key with this identifier exists. Use another identifier.
cer10.keyInvalid: The public key does not match the key service’s key, or is not P-256. Check the public key.

cer10.retireText: It still verifies what it signed.
